parsed.same_study_reason: Both lists concern estimating the welfare value of reducing farm-animal suffering using stated WTP/WTA scenarios, including whether those responses validly isolate altruistic animal-welfare preferences.

pairs.reason: Both question whether product-related WTP is a valid measure of animal-welfare preferences because it may incorporate non-welfare motives. A1 identifies concrete confounds in cultured-meat substitution WTP; B6 states the broader construct-validity concern across the study's measures.

Both argue that stated valuations may fail to isolate the value of reduced animal suffering because responses include other reactions to the scenario. B4 demonstrates this through the welfare-neutral anchor; A2 makes the broader point across several proposed WTP elicitation methods.

Both concern construct contamination in stated measures of willingness to pay for animal welfare. A2 details limitations of particular cultivated-meat, genetically modified animal, and welfare-label questions, whereas B6 frames the general concern that responses need not measure welfare judgments.

Both challenge using hypothetical WTP/WTA responses to identify the value of avoiding animal suffering. A2 focuses on preference and product/certification confounds, while B2 focuses on unvalidated aggregation, comparability, interpretation, and zero-point assumptions.
